title: Critical Discourse Analysis: van Dijk
short_description: Guidance for analyzing discourse, power, ideology, access, elite discourse, and group representation.

phases.title: Power and access
phases.description: Analyze who has access to discourse, who controls topics, and whose voice is authorized.
recommended_actions: Link actors to claims and features.

phases.title: Ideology and groups
phases.description: Analyze ingroup/outgroup construction, self-presentation, other-presentation, and dominance.
prompts: How are us and them constructed?

phases.title: Elite discourse
phases.description: Analyze how elite speakers, institutions, and media reproduce or challenge dominance.
prompts: What is treated as legitimate knowledge?
Who controls the definition of the situation?
Which group is evaluated positively or negatively?

concepts.description: Socially shaped representations through which people understand events and groups.
Power abuse or unequal control reproduced through discourse and institutions.
Patterns of speaking, being quoted, being spoken about, or being absent.

sources.apa: van Dijk, T. A. (1998). Ideology: A multidisciplinary approach. SAGE.
sources.note: Use for ideology, groups, and social cognition.

sources.apa: van Dijk, T. A. (2008). Discourse and power. Palgrave Macmillan.
sources.note: Use for power, dominance, elite discourse, and access.

sources.apa: van Dijk, T. A. (2009). Society and discourse: How social contexts influence text and talk. Cambridge University Press.
sources.note: Use for social context, mental models, and discourse-society links.
